kind: A data-scaling test at full size: the stack of fsp-lift2 and the Transformer of fsp-tf, each trained for 45,000, 90,000 and 180,000 updates with everything else unchanged, to measure how the gap moves per doubling of the training data where the race is run. One seed per length.
why: Daniel, 2026-11-26: "run the scaling test on weekend". Every full-size comparison so far is at one length, 90,000 updates, so it gives the gap's level and not its slope, and a level reached at one length means little if the gap widens with data. On the test bed it does: the delayed bed is 0.047 ahead at 6,000 updates and 0.054 behind at 24,000 (gap_with_data.json), and since 2026-11-22 designs are judged by the slope of the gap per doubling (data_scaling_long.json). Two changes since hold a constant gain with data on the bed (the full size's cell shape and power-law cells), and none has yet reversed the slope. This test measures the slope of the design that holds both, at full size.

arms.stack: fsp-lift2's recipe (full_size_lifted_loop_second.json): the looped stack, levels 2 to 8 twice (--stack-loop 2,8,2 --pulse-budget 507000 --pool-lifts-ceiling --granule-power 8), the inhibitory pool lifting the cells' ceiling and power-law cells, about 36 M parameters after the fork, peak rate 6e-4, code v18c (f876392). Three lengths: fsd-st-45k (new), fsp-lift2 at 90,000 (its own record; it starts on 2026-11-26 at 16:45Z) and fsd-st-180k (new).
arms.transformer: fsp-tf's recipe (full_size_best_rate_pair.json): 11 levels of width 512, 8 heads, SwiGLU feed-forward, rotary positions, LayerNorm, 34,752,000 parameters, peak rate 1.2e-3, code v17l (072eb90). Three lengths: fsd-tf-45k (new), fsp-tf at 90,000 (trained and scored: frozen test 1.07899, validation 1.10480) and fsd-tf-180k (new).

training: sched/bin/full-pair4.sh, which is full-pair3.sh with the run's length (STEPS) and its fork (FORK) as parameters; at 90,000 and 24,000 it runs exactly as full-pair3.sh, and without trainer flags as full-pair.sh, which trained fsp-tf. One cosine over the run's length with 1,000 warm-up updates; windows of 512 bytes in batches of 8 for the first 4/15 of the run (12,000 of 45,000; 24,000 of 90,000; 48,000 of 180,000), then forked onto the long stage (the stack on unbroken streams of windows of 2,048 with 128 knowledge cells a head and a reach of 2,048, the Transformer on windows of 2,048) to the run's end. 4,096 bytes an update throughout, so 184 M, 369 M and 737 M training bytes from the enwik8, C4 and PG-19 mixture at weights 2:1:1: enwik8's 90 M training bytes are seen about 1.0, 2.0 and 4.1 times, C4's 134 M about 0.34, 0.69 and 1.4 times, PG-19's 68 M about 0.68, 1.35 and 2.7 times. Seed 20001; each model at the peak rate full_size_rate_pilot chose for 90,000 updates; every other setting as at 90,000. Scheduler jobs with MPS=0 and GPU_MEM=85, each alone on its GPU: on GPU 1 fsd-tf-45k, fsd-tf-180k and fsd-st-45k in that order after fsp-lift and the night's pilots; on GPU 0 fsd-st-180k after fsp-lift2. So that both stacks run alone, every other job waiting for GPU 0 now starts after fsd-st-180k (they had no guard against starting beside fsp-lift2). Expected: the GPU-1 runs done on Saturday 2026-11-28, fsd-st-180k (about 35 hours with its scoring) on Sunday 2026-11-29, all within the weekend window.
measure: At each length as full_size_lifted_loop_second.json: the stack read as a stream over the full enwik8 test and validation splits at the reach chosen on the first 1,000,000 validation bytes (the trained 2,048 or 8,192), with fast output synapses at 2^24 on the cells of all 18 passes (taught) and without; the Transformer in windows of 2,048 with 2,032 bytes of history, frozen and with fast synapses at 0.07. The gap at a length is the stack's taught score less the Transformer's frozen score, paired piece by piece (experiments/compare_stream_scores.py), on test and on validation. The slope per doubling is the change of the gap from 45,000 to 90,000 and from 90,000 to 180,000. Beside them: each model's own scores at the three lengths, the gap against the Transformer taught at 0.07, the gap split by context (experiments/gap_by_piece.py, near 2,032, far 8,192), the trainers' validation curves, the pulses a byte and the training times.
reading: (1) The gap shrinks with data at full size if it falls by at least 0.005 from 45,000 to 90,000 and again from 90,000 to 180,000, on test and on validation. It grows with data if it rises by at least 0.005 at both doublings on both splits. It holds level if every change is within 0.005. Anything else is mixed and is reported as it is. The mark is per doubling: the byte-paired intervals are reported, but with one seed per length the seeds' spread (0.003 to 0.005 on the test bed) is not measured, and the mark is set above it. (2) If the gap shrinks, its mean change per doubling is extrapolated to the length at which it would close, as an extrapolation and not a claim, and the next step is longer training and more data for both models. If it grows, the stack must change how it learns from data before it is scaled, and the full-size work turns to the slope. If it holds level, the gap is an offset that more data does not close, and the work stays on its level. (3) Repeated data: if a model's validation score at 180,000 is worse than at 90,000, it overfits the repeated mixture, and the doubling from 90,000 to 180,000 is reported as a measure of repeated data rather than of more data; the doubling from 45,000 to 90,000 then carries the reading alone. (4) If fsp-lift2 fails or is not scored by its record, the slope is read from 45,000 to 180,000 as two doublings, half the change for each. (5) If the stack's taught score is below the Transformer's frozen score at any length with the paired interval below zero on both splits, that is reported as a win at that length, by full_size_best_rate_pair.json's reading, with the pulses a byte.
seen_before_recording: fsp-tf's scores at 90,000 (frozen test 1.07899, validation 1.10480; taught at 0.07, 1.07714 and 1.10442) and its training log; fsp-lift's training log to 75,750 updates; the test bed's data-scaling records. A dry run of full-pair4.sh with the trainer replaced by echo, which printed its commands for 45,000 and 180,000 updates; nothing trained and its folders were removed. fsp-lift2 has not started, and no arm of this record has trained.

amendment.change: Since this record was written, reads by age were built (696f5ef, d3ed961, bfaebd2): a stream's race read is worked out against the cells within its reach instead of every cell of its table, the same pulses with less work. On the server's GPU a stream-stage update of this stack takes 0.43 s instead of 0.81 s, which shortens fsd-st-45k from about 11 hours to about 6 and fsd-st-180k from about 35 to about 20. fsd-st-45k and fsd-st-180k therefore train and are scored on the code copy v18k (bfaebd2) instead of v18c if its CUDA check, queued alone on GPU 1 after fsp-lift (speed-check-v18k), finds (i) both windows of a full-size stream firing the same spikes by age as by cell, with the same loss, and (ii) one update's gradients by age within 1e-4 of each tensor's largest entry of the gradients by cell. Otherwise both stay on v18c as registered. Why this leaves the test as it was: v18k computes v18c's forward pass spike for spike, and a trained model is scored by both copies to the same bit; the gradients differ only in the order of float32 sums (3.4e-6 of the largest entry in the CUDA check of 696f5ef, 3.1e-6 on the CPU), and the check reports beside them how far two runs of the same read differ on CUDA, where the backward pass adds in no fixed order. fsp-lift2, the 90,000-update point, stays on v18c, and the Transformer arms are untouched. Everything else is as registered; the training times reported beside the scores are then v18k's for the two new stacks.
amendment.seen_before_amendment: No arm of this record has trained; fsp-lift2 started at 16:45Z and none of its log has been read. The speed profiles of v18c and of 696f5ef on GPU 1 at 16:45Z (by cell 0.81 s an update; by age 0.43, 0.46 and 0.53 s in blocks of 2,048, 512 and 256) and the CUDA check of 696f5ef in blocks of 256 (0 of 1,048,576 counts differ, gradients within 3.4e-6); the CPU tests of bfaebd2; and a CPU check that v18k scores fsp-loop's averaged weights, taught at 2^24 on its 18 passes, on the first 8,192 test bytes as two streams, to the same bits as v18c (1.206176 bpb, the bits files identical).

amendment_2.change: A further step of the same kind, written before its check runs: fused race kernels (snnformer/race_kernel.py, 32adeb0) compute a read by age's race and the payload pulses it passes on a block of bytes against a block of cells at a time, writing only the race's growth, once, for its total, which PyTorch still sums in the same layout. fsd-st-45k and fsd-st-180k train and are scored with fused reads (on v18l's code with the fused reads switched on, a commit that changes nothing else) instead of v18k if the CUDA check queued after speed-check-v18k (race-kernel-check) finds (i) the kernels' tests passing on CUDA, (ii) both windows of a full-size stream firing the same spikes with fused reads as by age, with the same loss, (iii) one update's gradients within 1e-4 of each tensor's largest entry, and (iv) a stream-stage update taking at most 0.8 times as long as by age. Otherwise the first amendment decides between v18k and v18c as written. fsp-lift2 stays on v18c and the Transformer arms are untouched; everything else is as registered.
amendment_2.seen_before_amendment: As at the first amendment, and: the kernels' tests in Triton's CPU interpreter (24 passed: the same spikes, payload pulses and tapes as the read by age; gradients within 1e-4), and a CPU run of the full-size stack at windows of 32 bytes, in which fused reads fired the same spikes with the same loss as reads by age, gradients within 2.1e-6. No GPU run of the kernels, no arm of this record trained.
